sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: The Mesa Verde fishhook cactus is a small, usually solitary, pale green cactus of alkaline clay badlands in Colorado and New Mexico. Most stems are about 3–11 cm tall and 4–8 cm wide; exceptional plants reach roughly 18 × 10 cm. Its short straw-coloured radial spines do not hide the ribs.

sections.title: Flowers and conservation
sections.text: Cream to yellow flowers, sometimes pink, open at the stem tip in late April or early May and measure about 1–3.5 cm long. Green fruits turn tan as they mature. The species is federally threatened in the United States; no edible use is established in the sources consulted.
